May those gurus— who are skilled in ethics, devoted to the faultless, free from envy, incomparable, free from affliction, ever delighted in the stainless, and devoid of worldly desire— rejoice eternally.
They were peaceful, with tranquil minds, their sorrow and fear removed. || 39 ||
May those devoted to yoga rejoice, as well as those joined to the family yoga— the teachers, the initiates bound by the samaya, the practitioners, and the spiritual sons—
along with cows, the twice-born, young women, ascetics, and maidens.
May people devoted to their gurus practice with dedication in the Dharma. || 40 ||
May the families of practitioners, firmly established in the Self, rejoice;
may the curses of the Yoginīs fall upon the enemy of the covenant;
and may that indescribable state of Śāmbhavī, which is beyond all attainment, manifest.
In which [state], the lotus feet of the Guru alone are the truth. || 41 ||

Those which dwell in the stages of the sequence of the wheels (*cakra*), those which are situated within the channels (*nāḍī*), those which reside in the pores of the skin that have emerged from the body, and those which are established in the elements (*dhātu*);
those which dwell in the waves of the vital breaths of inhalation and exhalation, and those whose abode is the out-breath—
May these goddesses, who delight in devouring the faction of enemies and are worshipped by the Kaulas, rejoice! || 42 ||
Those goddesses who have arisen from the [five] families and dwell upon the earth; those deities who dwell in the waters;
those of eternally celebrated splendor who dwell in fire; those whose abode is the wind;
those who consist of the nectar of the sphere placed in the sky; and those who are omnipresent at all times—
May all those goddesses, devoted to the preservation of the family path, grant me peace. ||43||
Whether above the cosmic egg, or in heaven, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, or in the netherworld, in fire, in water, or in wind— wherever situated—
or having placed their feet upon sacred fields, seats, and secondary seats, [may they be worshipped] with incense, lamps, and other offerings.

May the goddesses, who are always pleased with us through the rite of the auspicious bali-offering and are worthy of worship by the lords of heroes, protect us. (44) Brahmā, Śrī, Śeṣa, Durgā, Guha, the Gaṇas, the Bhairavas, Kṣetrapālas and others, Vetālas, Ādityas, Rudras, the Planets, Vasus, Manus, Siddhas, Apsarases, Guhyakas, and so forth— [may they all protect us].
May all beings—the Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, Ṛṣis, Pitṛs, Yakṣas, Asuras, Kinnaras, and others;
the lords of Yogins, Cāraṇas, Kimpuruṣas, and the best of Munis—those who dwell upon the discus, protect [me].
May all the deities residing within the body, the elephant-faced ones, the lords of sacred fields (Kṣetrapālas), and the Bhairavas [protect me].
May the yoginīs, the vaṭukas, the yakṣas, the pitṛs, the bhūtas, the piśācas, the grahas,

and others who roam the earth, the sky, and the quarters, as well as the vetālas and ceṭakas, be satisfied; may they drink the beverage of this son of noble family, together with the lamp and the sacrificial porridge.
If the word of the Guru is indeed true; if the ancestors, the gods, and the Yoginīs are pleased; if the Supreme Deity exists; if the Vedas are indeed authoritative;
if the Śākta philosophy is valid; and if the Command (Ājñā) is indeed unfailing—then [act accordingly].
And may truth and the supreme Kaula dharma be mine; may victory be mine forever. (47)
May all practitioners rejoice; may those who defile the lineage be destroyed.
May the Śāmbhavī power reside within me, and may my Guru be forever gracious.
If this Goddess Bhairavī exists, if there is the teaching of Bhairava, and if this is the Kula-dharma, then may those who revile it perish! (49)
Salutations eternally to all those Yoginīs, by the power of whose command the three worlds are established.
May all the Mothers drink; may the best of the lineage drink;
may all the Bhairavas established within my body drink. (51)
May all the Mothers, the oceans, and the lords of the hosts, as well as the Yoginīs and the Kṣetrapālas who are established within my body, be satisfied. (52)
May the universe— from Śiva down to the earth, including all from Brahmā to a blade of grass,
and from the Fire of Time up to Śiva— be satisfied by this sacrifice.
Those who stand at the gates of the jeweled pavilion, throughout the glorious Nandana grove,

those situated in empty houses, monasteries, caves, and hermitages, those dwelling in the sky or in cremation grounds, those located at wells, those at crossroads, and those stationed at junctions— [all these are present].
May they accept [these offerings] from the lotus, the one that brings wealth, the banner, and the flower; and may they protect you. || 54 ||
O Dear One, having recited [the mantra] and lifted up the vessel of worship, the Guru should then bestow the prasāda upon his disciple, O Mistress of the Kula. (55)
The performance of one's own desired activities is proclaimed as the "Mature End" (*prauḍhānta*).
O Goddess, when the circle of yogis and the circle of yoginīs are delighted, having been uplifted by that Mature End, bliss is said to arise in due order. (56)
When heroes have ascended to that state, there exists neither what should be done nor what should not be done;
"Will alone is the perfection of the scriptures"—such is the command of the Supreme Goddess.
In that regard, O beautiful goddess, whatever action is performed, whether auspicious or inauspicious, all of it arises for the sake of pleasing the deity.
Idle chatter is the fruit of recitation; drowsiness gives rise to meditative absorption.
O Goddess, transformation is worship; this is declared to be the offering to Bhairavī. || 59 ||
Liberation occurs through union with Śakti; the hymn was spoken at that time;
the ritual placement (nyāsa) is the touching of the limbs; and the meal is the act of offering oblations.

O Īśānī, gazing is meditation, and lying down is prostration; whatever various activities are performed during that state of exaltation are true rites. He who deliberates upon what ought and ought not to be done is a sinner.
The heroes situated within this wheel are to be known as supreme yogins,
by whom men directly attain the very form of Bhairava.
Mutual greeting is supreme bliss; falling [in prostration] increases wisdom;
playing flutes, lutes, and other instruments, as well as composing poetry and the like, [are also beneficial]. || 63 ||
Crying, speaking, falling down, rising up, yawning, walking, and physical transformation— O Goddess, these are designated as "yoga."
In this wheel, O Goddess, the heroes and the heroines, slow with passion, perform according to their inspiration and as it arises in their minds. 65.
Forgetting what they intended to say, they ask those standing nearby in a low voice;
and placing their bowls in their mouths, they remain there dejected.
Just as a woman, thinking her own man to be intoxicated, takes hold of another lover, so too does the man, filled with the intense exhilaration of passion. (67)
Out of delusion, a man embraces another man who is not a woman; the bewildered girl asks her own husband: "Who are you? Who am I? And who are these others? (68)
"What task have we come for? For what purpose are we stationed here?
Alas, is this a garden, or a house, or perhaps a courtyard? (69)
Filling their mouths with wine, the women make their lovers drink;
having placed a snack in their own mouths, they transfer it into the mouths of their lovers.
O Śāmbhavī, the yogins take up one another’s bowls and condiments;
placing vessels of wine upon their heads, they dance. (71)
The Kula-śaktis dance, their songs sung in indistinct syllables amidst the dense darkness of ignorance, with the placement of their steps faltering.
Yogins intoxicated by pride fall into the lap of negligence; and yoginīs agitated by pride fall upon men. (73)
O Mistress of the Clan, they fulfill each other's desires completely and perform various such activities. (74)
When, having abandoned the transformation of the mind, an inner radiance proceeds,
then the preeminent among yogis partake in the state of divinity.
O Mistress of the Kula, the Yoginīs undoubtedly destroy that fool-minded person who reviles the Kaulikas who are possessed by Bhairava. (76)
One should neither revile nor laugh at anyone within the circle who is languid from the intoxication of wine;
nor should one ever disclose to outsiders any news concerning those within this circle.
One should not commit malice toward them, nor should one act harmfully toward them;
with devotion one should honor them and protect them with great effort. (78)
Having seen those who are agitated by intoxication, one should regard them with the thought that they are deities;
he who rejoices in them and honors them with devotion shall go to the state of the Yoginīs.
O Dear One, that Kaulika who beholds such a wheel with devotion shall obtain the fruit of ten million vows, pilgrimages, austerities, gifts, and sacrifices.
In the wheel worshipped by heroes, which is known as Unmanā, there is the rising and falling of the mind, and repeated fainting, upon the manifestation of that state called Unmanā. (81)
O Mistress of the Family, those two who are devoted to the performance of their duties and who long for the contemplation of the Supreme Brahman shall remain united for a long time.
The state of being without control over the body and the senses is called *samavasthā*.
When that which is designated as *samavasthā* arises, one becomes equal [to all]. (83)
This supreme mūrcchanā arises, having the nature of the supreme mantra;
for they know that proximity to mūrcchanā is the supreme root of liberation. (84)
With the internal object as the focus and the gaze directed outward, free from the opening and closing of the eyes—this is the Śāmbhavī Mudrā, hidden in all the Tantras. (85)
Transcending all, the ego is eternally of the nature of aesthetic equilibrium (sāmarasya); those heroes who delight in this are Śivas themselves—of this there is no doubt. (86)
When men are devoted to meditation upon their own Self, they know something indescribable; that which is then experienced is a supreme bliss that cannot be expressed in words.
Just as when drinking milk, the sugar-candy itself is experienced directly;
such and such happiness cannot be described in words.
That which is perceived through horripilation and other signs is called meditation on Brahman. (88)
That supreme bliss which exists in meditation and brings about divine possession, I am unable to describe even when awakened and composed in samādhi. (89)
Men of virtuous deeds who are devoted to the supreme bliss of meditation on Brahman grieve when that [moment] has passed away even for an instant, their own splendor having been destroyed.

O Mistress of the Kula, for your devotees who possess the sevenfold ecstasy, there is a great fruit: the eight signs of realization arising from the knowledge of the three times, and the eight states beginning with trembling; of this there is no doubt. (91)
What need is there for much speaking here? Having attained the eight supernatural powers beginning with *aṇiman*, they have long served the palace, having reached the rank of doorkeepers.
Whatever auspicious qualities belong to the Supreme Lord whose body has five faces,
those same qualities are gathered within the knower of the Kula-reality through the knowledge of reality.
The beginning, the youthful stage, the adolescent, and the mature;
that which follows them is called waking, while the state beyond the mind (unmanā) is called dreaming.
The state of equilibrium is deep sleep, which is joined with the three states;
he who knows the sevenfold manifestation is liberated and is a Kaulika. (95)
When the Bhairavī-cakra is active, all castes are twice-born;
when the Bhairavī-cakra has ceased, all castes are distinct once more.
Whether woman, man, eunuch, outcaste, or the best of the twice-born—there is no distinction whatsoever in this wheel; all are remembered as equal to Śiva. || 97 ||
Just as the waters of rivers such as the Narmadā attain oneness upon reaching the Gaṅgā,
so too do all human beings attain oneness within the center of the Śrīcakra.
Just as water mixed with milk becomes milk itself, so too within the Śrīcakra, no distinction of caste exists. || 99 ||
Just as there are no gods other than those in the meritorious worlds such as Svarga, so too within the Cakra, all deities are merely human beings. 100.
There is no distinction of caste in this wheel; all are remembered as equal to Śiva.
Indeed, it is established even in the Veda, for Brahmā himself has declared that all are indeed Brahman. (101)
What need is there for much speaking here, O Kuleśvarī? Within the circle, all men are my own form and all women are your own form, my beloved.
O Mistress of the Kula, I swear that the Yoginīs shall devour that deluded soul who creates distinctions of caste within the center of the Cakra. 103.
One should have one of the women and one of the men sit separately in their respective places, or else, having formed a pair, he should have them sit down together in due order.
O Dear One, whether in the form of a line or properly in the form of a circle, one should worship them all in the center of the wheel with the thought that they are Śiva and Śakti. || 105 ||
Just as we two, Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, are inseparable, or as Vāṇī and the Creator are, so too is the Hero together with Śakti. || 106 ||
O beautiful woman, I am not satisfied even by thousands of jars of honey or hundreds of loads of meat, without the nectar of the vulva and the phallus.
This world bears neither the mark of a wheel, nor the mark of a lotus, nor the mark of a cow-pen;
it bears the marks of the *liṅga* and the *bhaga*, and therefore its essence consists of Śakti and Śiva.
At whatever time the union of Śiva and Śakti arises, that is the twilight for those established in Kula; it is prescribed as their meditative absorption (samādhi).
A lustful man should not approach a woman who desires him if she has not been initiated;
however, he may approach a woman who has been purified by the immediate consecration, for that is what is prescribed.
Thus, O Mistress of Kula, the distinctions regarding the drinking of the radiance of the three principles and so forth have been taught in brief. What more do you wish to hear? 111.

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Distinctions Concerning the Drinking of the Three Principles and Other Matters," in the *Ūrdhvāmnāya-tantra*, within the fifth section of the *Śrī-kulārṇava*, the great secret, the supreme among all scriptures, which contains one hundred and twenty-five thousand verses and concerns the gateway to liberation through Nirvāṇa. 8.
Now begins the ninth chapter.
The venerable Goddess said:
"O Lord of the Kula, I desire to hear about Yoga and the characteristics of the masters of Yoga."
O ocean of compassion, tell me the fruit of worship performed out of devotion to one's own family lineage.
The Lord said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall declare that which you ask of me;
by the mere hearing of it, Yoga becomes manifest in person.
Meditation is said to be of two kinds, distinguished as gross and subtle;
they say that which has form is gross, while that which is formless is subtle.
Some, whose minds are fixed on a stable object, describe coarse meditation;
yet when the mind is immovable even toward the coarse, it shall likewise be immovable toward the subtle.
One should meditate upon the Supreme Lord, who is devoid of hands, feet, belly, face, and so forth; who consists of all splendor; and who is partless, being existence, consciousness, and bliss.
It neither rises nor sets; it neither increases nor wanes.
It shines by itself, illuminating all other things without any external means.
Infinite, having transcended the nature of form, pure existence alone, beyond the range of the senses, and perceivable by the mind alone—that knowledge is designated as Brahman. (7)
With the movement of the vital breaths completely ceased, as motionless as a stone, the yogi who knows the sole abode of the Supreme Life is called a knower of yoga. 8.
That which here [in this state] is without appearance, remaining like a motionless ocean, empty of its own nature—that is called meditation (dhyāna) and is designated as concentration (samādhi). 9.
The reality does not reveal itself merely through thinking about it;
when the reality reveals itself of its own accord, one becomes identical with it at that very moment.
He who remains like one asleep even during the states of dreaming and waking, and is devoid of inhalation and exhalation—he is certainly liberated. (11)
With the collection of sense organs rendered motionless and the mind and breath dissolved into one's own Self, he who remains as if truly dead is called "liberated while living" (jīvanmukta). 12.
He does not hear, nor does he smell; he does not touch, nor does he see;
he does not know pleasure or pain, and his mind does not form conceptual constructions. 13.
He knows nothing at all, nor does he perceive anything, like a piece of wood;
thus, with his self dissolved in Śiva, he is said here to be established in samādhi.

Just as water poured into water, milk into milk, or ghee into ghee becomes indistinguishable, so too is the relationship between the individual self (jīvātman) and the supreme self (paramātman). || 15 ||
Just as even an insect becomes like a bee through the power of meditation, so too may a person become one with Brahman through the power of samādhi. || 16 ||
Just as ghee extracted from milk, once thrown back into it, is not as it was before,
so too is the self said here to be separated from its qualities.
Just as one situated in dense darkness sees nothing here at all, so too the yogi, for whom [reality] is unperceivable, does not see conceptual proliferation (prapañca) whatsoever. 18.
Just as one does not perceive any conceptual proliferation at the time of closing the eyes, so too it should be when opening them; this is the characteristic of such meditation. || 19 ||
Just as an ordinary person perceives the itching of his own body,
so too does he who is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman perceive the activities of the entire universe.
When the supreme reality— transcending the castes and indeed changeless— is known,
the mantras together with the lords of mantras truly enter into the state of servitude.
For one who is established in the singular state of the Self, whatever movement there is is its worship;
whatever speech there is is the true mantra; and whatever gaze there is is its meditation.
When the identification with the body has dissolved and the Supreme Self is realized, wherever the mind goes, there it is in a state of meditative absorption (samādhi). || 23 ||
The knot of the heart is severed, all doubts are cut asunder, and one's karmas are exhausted when that Supreme Self is seen. 24.
When the Lord of Yogins attained that stainless, supreme state,
even the status of gods and asuras, though it had been attained, was no longer grasped.
For one who perceives that which is all-pervading, peaceful, consisting of bliss, and imperishable, there remains nothing further to be known that has not already been attained. (26)

O Goddess, when knowledge and discernment have been attained, when the object of knowledge is established in the heart, and when the state of peace has been reached, there is neither yoga nor even dhāraṇā.
Once the Supreme Brahman is realized, there is no need for all the various observances;
what use is a palm-leaf fan once the breeze from the Malaya mountains has been obtained? (28)
For those who perceive "Om" within themselves, there is no binding by the mouth, nor indeed any binding by the nose; there is neither restraint (yama) nor observance (niyama).
Yoga is not [attained] through the lotus posture, nor by gazing at the tip of the nose;
those proficient in yoga declare that yoga is the unification of the individual soul (jīva) and the Self (ātman). 30.
Indeed, for those who meditate here with supreme faith for even a single moment,
the limit of the very great merit that arises cannot be calculated.
He who performs self-reflection for even a moment, thinking "I am Brahman," shall destroy all sin, just as the rising sun destroys darkness.
Whatever fruit is obtained from vows, sacrifices, austerities, pilgrimages, charity, and the worship of deities, the knower of reality obtains that multiplied ten millionfold. || 33 ||
The supreme state is the innate (sahaja); the middling is meditative concentration and retention;
recitation and praise are the inferior; and fire-offerings and ritual worship are the lowest of the low.
Reflection on reality is the highest; reflection on recitation is middling; reflection on the scriptures is to be known as low; and reflection on worldly affairs is the lowest of the low. (35)
Praise is equal to ten million acts of worship; recitation is equal to ten million praises;
meditation is equal to ten million recitations; and absorption is equal to ten million meditations. || 36 ||
For there is no mantra higher than meditation, no deity higher than the Self,
no worship higher than contemplation, and indeed no fruit higher than contentment.
Non-action alone is the supreme worship; silence alone is the supreme recitation;
non-thinking alone is the supreme meditation; and desirelessness alone is the supreme fruit. || 38 ||
A yogi should constantly perform his twilight devotions without mantras or water, his austerity without offerings or fire-oblations, and his worship without ritual services. (39)
Free from attachment and free from clinging, having transcended the latent impressions of limiting conditions, and immersed in his own true nature—he is the yogi who knows the supreme reality. 40.
O Goddess, the body is the temple; the living soul is the deity, Sadāśiva.
One should discard the ritual remains of ignorance and worship with the realization of "I am He. 41.
The individual soul (jīva) is Śiva, and Śiva is the individual soul; that individual soul is Śiva alone when free [from bonds].
Bound by fetters, it is known as the individual soul; released from fetters, it is Sadāśiva.
Just as rice remains bound by its husk but becomes pure grain when the husk is absent,
so the individual soul (jīva) is known to be bound by karma, while Sadāśiva is eternally liberated from karma.
The Lord dwells as fire in the hearts of the wise and as the deity in the minds of the contemplative;
He resides in images for the unawakened, and everywhere for those who have realized the Self.
He who remains equanimous amidst blame and praise, cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and toward enemies and friends— that lord of yogis is free from both elation and dejection.
Free from desire, eternally contented, viewing all with equanimity, and having conquered the senses,
the yogi who knows the supreme reality dwells in the body like a traveler in a foreign land.
Free from conceptualization, free from discursive thought, untainted by the impressions of limiting adjuncts,
and immersed in his own true nature— that yogi is the knower of the supreme reality.
Just as those who are lame, blind, deaf, impotent, insane, dull-witted, and so forth dwell [in the world], O Mistress of the Kula, so too does the yogi who knows reality. || 48 ||
He who abides, filled with the supreme bliss arising from the five mudrās, is indeed the lord of yogins; he beholds the Self within the self.
O beloved, that very pleasure which arises from attachment to women with fleshly bodies is liberation for the wise, but for the ignorant it is a sin. 50.
He who always delights in meat and wine, who always contemplates the feet [of the Guru], and who is always free from doubt—he is called a Kula-yogin. (51)
Drinking liquor and eating meat, devoted to acting according to my own will,
I shall dwell happily, contemplating the identity of these two.
He whose mouth is devoid of the fragrance of the savory offerings of food must undergo penance and be shunned; he is indeed a mere beast, without a doubt. (53)
As long as there is the scent of impurity, even Paśupati himself is but a beast;
without the scent of the flesh of the bee (alimāṃsa), one is truly a beast before Paśupati.
In this world, that which is low is [regarded as] high, and that which is high in the world is low;
such is the path of the Kula taught by the great-souled Bhairava. (55)
O Mistress of the Kula, for those of the Kaula lineage, improper conduct is always right conduct, and what should not be done is the highest duty; even untruth becomes truth. 56.

O Mistress of the Kula, for the followers of the Kaula path, even that which is undrinkable becomes drinkable, even that which is unfit to be eaten becomes edible, and even that which is unapproachable becomes approachable. (57)
O Mistress of the Kula, for those of the Kaula lineage, there is neither injunction nor prohibition, neither merit nor sin, neither heaven nor indeed hell. (58)
O Leader of the Clan, the weavers— who are ignorant yet act as if they possess higher knowledge, who are poor yet act as if they possess wealth, and who flourish even though they are ruined— thrive.
Even enemies become friends, and kings serve them face to face;
all people act as kinsmen to the weavers, O Mistress of the Kula. (60)
O Mistress of the Kula, for the followers of the Kaula path, those who are averse become well-disposed, all speak with affection, and even those who cause harm act as supporters.
O Mistress of the Kula, for the Kaulikas, the attributeless appears as possessing attributes, the unmanifested becomes well-manifested, and even non-dharmas function as dharma. 62.
O Goddess, for the Kaulikas, O Mistress of the Family, death acts as a physician, their home becomes heaven itself, and union with women becomes merit. (63)
O Beloved, what is the use of saying more here? O lords of the kula-yogins, they shall always achieve their intentions; no doubt should be entertained in this matter.
O Mistress of the Kula, the Kulayogin may dwell in any hermitage whatsoever, assuming any guise whatever and remaining unobserved by anyone. 65.
Yogins, acting for the benefit of humanity through various guises, wander this earth with their true nature remaining unrecognized. (66)
O Mistress of the Kula, they do not destroy the self-knowledge even once;
they may dwell in the midst of the world like one who is insane, mute, or dull-witted.
Just as in the world the moon and sun are unperceivable in the sky due to their conjunction with the stars and planets, so too is the conduct of yogins.
O Goddess, just as the path of birds in the sky or of aquatic creatures in the water cannot be seen, even so is the conduct of yogins.
Those proficient in the noble yoga appear as if non-existent; they act like the ignorant toward what is dear; and they are seen like commoners. (70)
Just as people might despise him so that they do not associate with him at all and do not say anything to him, in that same manner the yogi conducts himself. (71)
O Maheśvarī, though liberated, the Kula-yogin should play like a child, move like one who is dull-witted, and speak like one who is mad. (72)
Just as this world laughs, feels disgust, and reviles, and turns away upon seeing [a person] from afar, so does the yogi conduct himself. (73)

Sometimes appearing as a disciplined sage, sometimes as one who has fallen from his vows, and sometimes like a ghost or a piśāca, the yogī should wander upon the surface of the earth assuming various guises.
The yogi enjoys worldly pleasures for the benefit of the world, not out of desire;
bestowing grace upon all people, he may sport upon the surface of the earth.
Just as the sun completely dries up [everything], and just as fire consumes all enjoyments,
so too the yogi, having experienced all enjoyments, is not defiled by sins.
Just as the wind touches everything and just as space is all-pervading,
and just as all those who have bathed in a river are pure, so too is the yogi always pure.

Just as water that has reached a village becomes pure when joined with a river, so too food and other items from the house of a Mleccha become pure once they have passed through the hand of a yogi. 78.
O Goddess of the Gods, that which those expert in the knowledge of the Kula practice is alone to be honored by the wise who desire their own welfare. (79)
That upon which the lords of yoga move is considered the supreme path;
indeed, that from which the sun rises is called the eastern direction. (80)
Wherever the elephant goes, there the path shall be;
wherever the excellent Kulayogin goes, O Kuleśvarī, that is the path. 81.
Who is capable of making a crooked river straight, or of obstructing its current? Who is able to restrain one who wanders at will and is peaceful? (82)
Just as one endowed with the power of mantras is not seen by means of toys,
so too the man of knowledge, sporting with the serpents of the senses, is not seen.
Those who are content with the cessation of suffering, free from the pairs of opposites, devoid of envy,
devoted to their lineage and knowledge, and peaceful— they are your devotees, and they are the Kaulikas.

Those who speak the truth, who are free from intoxication, anger, hypocrisy, desire, and egoism; those Kaulika leaders who are steady and not subject to the power of the senses—[they are the true practitioners]. 85.

O Goddess, those whose hair stands on end and whose voices become choked with emotion when their lineage is being recited, and from whom tears of joy fall—they are declared to be the best of the Kaulikas. (86)
"The family dharma proclaimed by Śiva is superior to all dharmas in the world"—those whose intellects are thus resolved have been declared to you as the best of the Kaulikas. (87)
O Dear One, he who knows the reality of the Kula, is proficient in the Kula scriptures, and is devoted to the worship of the Kula—he alone is a Kaulika, and no other. 88.
He who becomes joyful upon seeing those devoted to the Kula, who possess Kula-knowledge, and who observe Kula-conduct and Kula-vows—that Kaulika is dear to me. (89)
One who knows the reality of the three principles, the feet of Śrī, and the meaning of the root mantra,
and who is devoted to the deity and the guru, becomes a Kaulika through initiation.
The sight of the family preceptor is difficult to obtain in all the worlds;
it is attained only through the full ripening of merits, O dear one, and not otherwise. (91)
Whether remembered, praised, seen, saluted, or even addressed, he who is the best of family traditions purifies—even a Cāṇḍāla—if encountered by chance. (92)
Whether he be omniscient or a fool, whether he be superior or even inferior— O Goddess, wherever there is one who possesses the knowledge of the Kula, there I am also, together with you.
I do not dwell on Kailāsa, nor on Meru, nor in a palace;
O beautiful lady, I reside wherever those who possess noble lineage abide.
One must travel even a very great distance to where there is a person devoted to Maheśvara;
for I am truly present there, and he should be seen with diligent effort. 95.
O Dear One, even if situated very far away, the family preceptor (kuladeśika) is to be seen;
whereas one who is nearby but is a mere beast (paśu) is not to be seen.
The land where one who possesses the knowledge of the Kula resides partakes in merit;
by seeing and worshipping him, one may uplift twenty-one generations of one's lineage.
Beholding a knower of the lineage residing in the house of their own spiritual succession, the ancestors declare: "We shall go to the supreme goal. (98)
The ancestors find comfort, like farmers at a timely rain, thinking:
"May there be a son or a grandson born in our lineage who shall be a follower of the Kula. (99)
O beloved, that man in this world is indeed blessed and his impurities are destroyed, to whose presence the family preceptors approach with joy. (100)
O Goddess, when the lord of the Kaulikas arrives at the abode of the Kaulikas, the Yoginīs come joyfully together with the Yogins. (101)
Having entered [the assembly], the ancestral deities say to the lord of the Kula-yogins:
"Therefore, one should worship with devotion those who are devoted to the knowledge of the Kula. (102)
O Goddess, those who, having worshipped you, do not worship your devotees, are the most sinful; they do not become recipients of your grace. (103)
O lotus-eyed one, the food offering placed before you has been accepted by you merely by your sight; I shall now taste the flavors from the tip of the devotee's tongue.
O Goddess, by worshipping your devotees, I am worshipped; of this there is no doubt.
Therefore, one who desires my favor should worship only your devotees. (105)
Whatever is performed by those devoted to the Kula becomes performed for the gods; all the gods are fond of the Kula, therefore one should worship the Kaulika. 106.
O Pārvatī, I am not so well-pleased when worshipped with devotion elsewhere as I am when properly worshipped by a supreme Kaulika.
O Dear One, that fruit which the lords of the Kaulas obtain through worship, they would not attain even through pilgrimages, austerities, gifts, sacrifices, or vows. 108.
O Mother, whatever has been given, sacrificed, offered in fire, performed as austerity, worshipped,
or recited becomes fruitless for a Kaulika who shows contempt for one who knows the Kula.
O Goddess, that house is a cremation ground and he is a sinner, the lowest of dog-cookers,
who enters a family but does not know its dharma or traditional conduct.
O Goddess, that gift which is bestowed upon another after abandoning those who belong to one's own family is fruitless; moreover, the giver shall go to hell. (111)
Just as water in a broken vessel, like a seed sown upon a stone,
or like an oblation poured into ashes— such is a gift given to one who does not belong to the Kaula tradition.
Whatever little one may give with affection to a Kulayogin according to one's ability, especially on the special lunar days— the fruit of that cannot even be described.

O Goddess, he who, having personally invited those possessing knowledge of the lineage on an auspicious day, honors them with the thought that they are deities, using perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice grains, and other offerings; || 114 ||
One should satisfy them with true devotion by means of the five mudrās, beginning with wine;
when they are satisfied, I am satisfied, and all the deities shall be satisfied. (115)
O Goddess of Gods, the merit of one who gives his sister, daughter, or wife to a yogin of noble lineage who is intoxicated with honey cannot be calculated. || 116 ||
Without being dug or planted, and without effort, it has grown; it is the provision for the journey to the next world, and even in the *vīracakra* [battle], this honey has been drunk. 117.
Indeed, the family wealth of one who is joined with evil conduct and excluded from all the world becomes drunk by the lords of the Kula-yogins. 118.
O beloved, in whatever land a hero devoted to the worship of his lineage resides, that land itself becomes purified; how much more so those who dwell within that city!
When the Lord of the Kaulas has eaten even once, the merit becomes ten millionfold;
how much more so when he has eaten many times—that merit cannot even be calculated.
Therefore, with every effort, in all circumstances, and at all times, one should be devoted to the family dharma and worship those who possess knowledge of the family. 121.
Whether one is wise or ignorant, as long as the body is sustained,
the conduct of one's caste and stage of life must be observed for the sake of liberation from karma.
When ignorance has been uprooted by knowledge through action, one attains the state of Śiva;
through that very state in Śiva, liberation occurs. Therefore, one should perform action.
One should perform blameless actions or carry out the obligatory duties;
liberated from [the bondage of] karma and desiring happiness, one who is established in action shall attain bliss. (124)
It is not possible for one who bears a body to completely renounce all actions;
however, he who renounces the fruit of action is called a renunciant.
One should reflect that it is the instruments (karaṇas) which engage in their respective functions;
he who acts while casting aside the sense of "I" is not defiled. 126.
Actions performed immediately after the attainment of knowledge do not touch the knower of reality, just as water does not touch a lotus leaf.
For one who is established in that [Brahman], meritorious and demeritorious actions go to destruction;
nor indeed are they tainted, even when being performed again.

O Dear One, he who delights in the knowledge of reality—the innate bliss that has arisen—and who has completely abandoned all conceptual constructions, that wise man should renounce ritual action. 129.
O beloved, those fools who have pointlessly abandoned the ritual section (karmakāṇḍa) are heretics who consider themselves wise; they go to hell.
Just as a tree, having attained fruit, casts off its flower without longing,
so too the yogi, having attained the ultimate reality, should abandon the accumulation of karma.
Even by ten thousand horse-sacrifices and ten thousand killings of Brahmins,
those in whose hearts the Brahman resides are not smeared by merit or sin.
Whatever actions exist on earth are caused by the tongue and the organ of generation;
one who has renounced the tongue and the organ of generation—what will he do with action? (133)
Thus, O Mistress of the Kula, I have told you something of the yoga characterized by the Lord of Yogins in brief; what more do you wish to hear? (134)

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Establishment of Yoga," in the *Ūrdhvāmnāya-tantra*, within the fifth section of the *Śrīkulārṇava*, the great secret, the supreme among all scriptures, containing one hundred and twenty-five thousand verses, concerning the gateway to liberation and nirvāṇa. 9.
Now begins the tenth chapter.
The venerable Goddess said: "O Lord of the Kula, I desire to hear about the worship on special days."
O God, O Supreme Lord, tell me the fruit of that worship.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall declare that which you ask of me;
by the mere hearing of it, one is liberated from all sins.
The daily worship is the highest; the worship on festival days is middling;
the monthly worship is the lowest, O Goddess; beyond a month, one becomes a beast.

If, after one month, there is a desire for the animal victim to enter again, its worship should be performed with the prescribed substances, beginning with honey and so forth, and it should be initiated once more.
Wine, meat, fish, parched grain, and sexual union—
O Goddess, this group of five beginning with the letter 'ma' brings delight to the deity.
O Īśānī, the wise man should practice the five beginning with *mā* according to the prescribed rule for the pleasure of the deity; if he does so out of craving, he is a sinner.
The eighth day of the dark fortnight, the fourteenth day, the new moon, the full moon, and the sun’s transit— these are the five sacred festivals (parvan), and on those meritorious days as well.
When the birth-day of one's guru arrives, as well as that of one's guru’s guru, and likewise on the birth-day of ordinary people and others, [one should perform worship]. || 8 ||

And one should sacrifice upon the attainment of prosperity, upon obtaining gains, during initiations into austerity, vows, and festivals; upon visiting sacred seats (pīṭhas), heroic seats (vīrapīṭhas), and upon seeing one's own kinsmen.
When the preceptor arrives, when visiting holy fords or deities, and on such occasions as these, O Goddess of Gods, as well as on special festival days. || 10 ||
According to one's wealth, according to one's faith, according to the available materials, and what is appropriate;
according to the time and according to the place—one should thus perform the worship.
One should have the worship of the wheel performed according to the procedure prescribed by the teacher,
or one may perform the worship oneself, O Goddess, preceded by the worship of the Bindu.
He attains that world from which there is no return;
however, by failing to perform [his duty] out of delusion, the Kaulika incurs the curse of the deity.
Every month, every three months, every six months, or even once a year, one should worship the venerable Guru with devotion; when he is not present, one should worship his wife, sons, and so forth.
In his absence, one should satisfy a knower of the Kula, or his disciple, or another yogi, with Kula-substances, preceded by Kula-worship. 15.
O Goddess, in the face of diseases, calamities, faults, evil associations, or ill omens, one should worship the assembly of Yoginīs for the pacification of those defects.
O Kuleśvarī, O beloved, in that place where there is a Kulācārya who knows the truth of a single tradition, as well as three, four, or five Kaulika Śaktis; (17)
O Goddess, one may worship them either individually or in the form of couples;
O Queen of the Gods, they should be well-adorned with perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), and so forth,
as well as with various foods such as edibles and masticables, including meats, endowed with the six flavors.
If they dwell together, endowed with mature exultation,
that is called the Śrīcakra, and it is also termed the Vṛnda.
In the month of Āśvina, one should perform the worship of nine young maidens;
the practitioner, with a pure mind, should devoutly invite them in the morning.
O Goddess, having bathed and purified his soul, the minister should then perform the sequential worship of a girl who is one year old, captivating to the mind, and endowed with auspicious marks.
Having purified her through an oil massage and a bath, one should lead her to the hall of worship;
having seated the young girl in the presence of the deity, one should perform the worship. || 22 ||

One should satisfy her with perfumes, flowers, and the like, with incense and lamps that illuminate the lineage, with various delicacies, foods, drinks, and so forth, with milk, clarified butter, honey, and meat, and with fruits such as plantains and coconuts. || 23 ||

O Goddess, being himself endowed with power and joined with the intense radiance of the ultimate state, he should recite the mantra according to his capacity, either by increasing it by one syllable at a time or otherwise. (24)
Seeing a young girl adorned with ornaments, one should contemplate her as one's own chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā).
Then, having paid homage to her with the recognition that she is the deity, one should dismiss her. || 25 ||
On the second lunar day, one should worship those aged from one to two years;
likewise, on the lunar day, one should sacrifice to the maiden who has been fasted since the previous day.
On the ninth [day], girls from one year up to nine years of age are prescribed;
they are celebrated as the nine: Bālā, Śuddhā, Lalitā, Mālinī, Vasundharā, Sarasvatī, Ramā, Gaurī, and Durgā.

One should worship them individually with their names preceded by the three *tāra*s (om āḥ hūṃ), ending with *namaḥ*, followed by the word "deity," and finally the name itself in the dative case. || 28 ||
[He should worship] the Baṭuka, five years old, and the nine-year-old Gaṇeśvara, with perfumes, flowers, garments, and ornaments, according to the extent of his available wealth. || 29 ||
Having worshipped with the perception of them as deities, one should satisfy them with offerings,
free from stinginess regarding wealth, for the sake of accomplishing the fruit of one's own purpose.
One should recite [the mantra] for nine nights in a sequence of increasing by one each day;
O Goddess, one should offer the worship performed during the nine nights to the Goddess.
Having offered betel-leaf and a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), he should dismiss those young maidens;
thus should the worship of the nine maidens be performed every morning throughout the year.
He who performs this is a meritorious soul who shall attain the favor of the deity;
having fulfilled his heart's desire, he shall dwell in your presence.
Alternatively, O Pārvatī, one who knows the mantras should worship with devotion during the nine nights those beautiful young women who have reached the prime of youth. (34)
One should satisfy Hṛllekhā, Gaganā, Raktā, Mahocchuṣmā, Karālikā,
Icchā, Jñānā, Kriyā, Durgā, Baṭuka, and Gaṇeśvara, as before, with offerings such as meat and other substances.
O beloved, if they are satisfied and endowed with the radiance of the mature culmination,
then the practitioner, having attained satisfaction, shall dwell in your presence.
Thus, O Goddess, he who, restrained in his vows, should worship every year, or every six months, or every three months, or even month by month, O Beloved; || 37 ||
One should worship three, five, or seven [images] with the thought that they are deities;
such a person, whose self is enriched with all sovereign powers, shall become dear to us both.
O Kuleśānī, on a Friday, [one should worship] a beloved woman who has ascended the prime of youth, endowed with all auspicious marks, well-disposed, and charming. || 39 ||
O Goddess, having invited and summoned eight women from noble families who are in their menses and whose bodies have been purified by an oil massage and bathing, one should seat them upon the throne.

Having adorned oneself with perfumes, flowers, garments, and ornaments, one who knows the ritual procedure should further adorn oneself with perfumes, flowers, and so forth, O Mistress of the Kula. (41)
Having invoked the deity into that [liṅga], one should worship according to the sequence of nyāsa;
having performed the sequential worship, one should offer incense, lamps, and the lamps of the kula.

Having presented these with the perception that they are the deity itself, one should satisfy the Goddess with devotion using substances endowed with the six flavors, such as meats and various kinds of foods to be chewed or swallowed. (43)
Beholding her endowed with the radiance of mature youth, one should recite the mantra;
oneself, likewise endowed with the radiance of youth, remaining intent upon that meditation. (44)
Having offered the recitation and other rites one thousand and eight times with a mind free from agitation, he should then spend the night together with her.
O beloved, for one who worships according to this rite on the fifth, third, seventh, or ninth lunar days falling on a Friday, the merit cannot be calculated.
O Mistress of the Kula, he obtains the fruit of worshipping the four seats;
whatever is desired by his own mind, that he attains without a doubt. (47)
On the ninth day, one who knows the ritual procedure should likewise worship according to the injunction;
by honoring [the deity] with all hymns of praise, he shall attain great sovereignty.
One may also perform the worship of the Twins in Cancer or Capricorn;
or of Leo in Libra or Aries, O beloved, during all the solar transits.
Gaurī and Śiva, Ramā and Viṣṇu, Vāṇī and the Lotus-seated One (Brahmā),
Śacī and Indra, Rohiṇī and the Moon, Svāhā and Agni, and Prabhā and Ravi.
Having worshipped the nine couples— Bhadrakālī and Vīrabhadra, as well as Bhairavī and Bhairava— by means of the very same path previously described.

The knower of the ritual procedure, having worshipped each [deity] by its respective name preceded by the three *tāra*s (oṃ āḥ hrīḥ) and ending with *namaḥ*, should satisfy them with perfumes, flowers, and so forth, as well as with wine and other offerings.
One should also perform the rites for the couples (mithuna) joined with the radiance of the final stage of maturity.
When this is done, there is no doubt that the deities of the couples are pleased; O Goddess, they bestow their grace and grant one's heart's desire.
He who performs the worship of the Couple with devotion every year shall dwell in your world, endowed with all sovereign powers.
Then, O Goddess, on the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha,
having risen during the Brāhma-muhūrta and performed the ritual bath and the twilight devotions (saṃdhyā), || 55 ||
In a pleasant and secluded place, facing the eastern direction, the knower of the ritual, having adorned himself with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, [should perform the rite]. 56.
Having performed the previously mentioned ritual placements (nyāsa) and established himself in the state of the deity,
when the sun has slightly risen, he [should worship] his own chosen deity within its orb.
Having meditated thus, O Dear One, one should properly worship [the deity] along with the coverings according to the prescribed rite,
preceded by the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjā), using the sixteen types of offerings.
Then, having displayed the lamps of the lineage to Śiva in the form of the Guru,
[he offered] fish, meat, and other such items, together with various kinds of food and edibles, according to the prescribed rite.
O beloved, having offered the *arghya*, one should personally drink the remainder with devotion,
accompanied by the joy of youth and with a mind free from all impurities.
Meditating upon that maṇḍala and having recited the mantra of the Goddess one thousand and eight times,
he should offer that worship and then release the deity.
O Ambikā, beginning thus from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should perform the recitation and worship day by day until the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.
On the new moon day, O Goddess, one who is free from greed for wealth should worship the Śakti-kaulikās—three, five, seven, or nine of them. (63)
Thus, whoever should perform the worship of the rising sun for even a single month, the deity, being well-pleased with him, grants his desired fruit. (64)
O beloved, one should worship the God at midday and worship Him at evening;
he obtains that fruit and becomes dear to the Yoginīs.
He who, knowing the ritual procedure, worships Trisandhyā in this manner for just one month,
attains the desired accomplishment and wanders upon the earth like a god.
On the first day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, having avoided food during the day,
and having bathed and put on white garments, he should perform the evening twilight devotions.
Endowed with all the ritual materials according to the path prescribed for the worship of the Sun,
and accompanied by the exuberance of youth, he should meditate upon the deity residing in the moon.
One should recite the mantra with undistracted mind until the setting of the moon;
in this manner, one should worship every day until the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight.
On the full moon day, one should worship the Śakti-kaulikās according to one's ability;
he who performs such worship with devotion during the bright fortnight, O Dear One, [attains the fruit]. (70)
With his soul purified of all sins and endowed with all sovereign powers,
he shall dwell upon the earth like Śiva, uniquely honored by all the worlds.
Just as one performs worship during the bright fortnight, so too during the other fortnight;
he who acts according to the prescribed rule attains all desires.
Having enjoyed all pleasures here like a god, one of pleasing appearance attains union with the Yoginīs and Vīras; of this there is no doubt. (73)
Then, O Goddess, on the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika,
having bathed and sipped water, the pure-souled one should perform the nyāsas previously described.

While the world of living beings was fast asleep during the deep of night, he, with a joyful soul and provided with all the ritual materials, performed [the worship] according to the procedure prescribed for the preliminary worship. || 75 ||
O Pārvatī, having ignited a wick as thick as the ring finger with clarified butter,
[one should place it] upon a lotus of eight petals variegated with powders of five colors.
Having placed a lamp before a jar filled with honey and a beautiful bell-metal vessel, he should stand facing north. || 77 ||

Having meditated upon the Goddess together with her veil in the lamp, one should worship her according to the prescribed rite, while recollecting the deity situated in the lamp and filled with the radiance of youth. (78)
One should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times with undistracted mind;
O Ambikā, in this manner one should perform worship until the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.
On the day of the new moon, one should worship the Śaktis and Kaulikas with devotion;
when this is done, O Mistress of the Kula, the deities will attain satisfaction. (80)
With his every desire fulfilled and endowed with all sovereign powers, he shall move about at ease, honored as the foremost in all the worlds.
One who is capable should perform the worship of the eight groups of eight on a single day;
or else on eight days of eight [each], or on sixteen days, or likewise on thirty-two days, or on sixty-four days. || 82 ||
O Goddess, one should have it performed by the Guru, or by another who knows the Krama;
if he himself knows the Krama, he may perform it provided he is free from stinginess regarding wealth.
O Dear One, the eight roots consist of Brahmā and the others, as well as the Bhairavas beginning with Asitāṅga, proclaimed together with the eight pairs beginning with Maṅgalā.
These are renowned in the Kula tradition as arising from the eight roots;
one should worship the sixty-four pairs beginning with Akṣobhya.

According to the previously mentioned procedure, one should perform the rite with as much elaboration as one's means allow; one must not omit any step for the sake of accomplishing one's own desired purpose.

O Goddess, one should properly satisfy the couples with supreme devotion using perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), and so forth; with fish, meat, fermented liquors (āsava), and the like; and with various kinds of foodstuffs, both solid and soft, endowed with the six flavors. 87.
O Ambikā, one should perform the Śrīcakra until the culmination of the intense, final radiance.
O Goddess, he who performs this worship of the eight-times-eight [deities] even once— || 88 ||
He is worshipped by the deities beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa;
how much more so by humans and others, for he is like another Śiva in person.
By worshipping him, one who is praised by the host of the sixty-four Yoginīs shall dwell in your presence, free from rebirth.
O Supreme Goddess, there is no worship superior to this, which is the cause of delight for all the deities; this is the truth, there is no doubt.
O beloved, he who beholds such a wheel consisting of sixty-four [petals] with devotion shall obtain the fruit of ten million sacrifices, gifts, austerities, pilgrimages, and vows.
O Goddess, the king who performs the worship of the eight-aṣṭakas with devotion rules the earth as far as the four oceans; of this there is no doubt. (93)
One who knows the ritual procedure, O Kuleśvarī, should worship the fifty couples beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha according to the previously mentioned method.
For the sake of accomplishing the fruit of one's own purpose, free from stinginess regarding wealth, one should worship the couples endowed with the radiance of the mature culmination. 95.
When satisfied, they grant the desired fruit to the practitioner.
O Dear One, with his command unimpeded everywhere, he is honored like a god;
O Goddess, praised by the gods beginning with Brahmā, he shall dwell in your world.
By properly worshipping the pairs beginning with Keśava and Gaṇeśa, Kāma and others, as well as Śrīkaṇṭha and the rest, one certainly obtains that fruit.
O Dear One, whoever should perform this act of grace during the worship of the Ḍākinīs and others—whether every month, or once a year on their own birthday—[attains the fruit]. 98.
According to the previously mentioned procedure, to the extent of one's means, the knower of that ritual should satisfy [the deity] up until the culmination of the intense outpouring of joy. 99.
O Goddess, all the deities, being well-pleased, bestow their grace;
[the devotee] becomes free from all calamities and endowed with all sovereign powers. 100.
Praised by all in this world, may he live for a hundred autumns;
at the end of the body, he attains your world, of this there is no doubt. (101)

O Dear One, he who performs the worship of the messenger (dūtīyāga) according to the previously stated rule, with a mind free from conceptual construction and endowed with the nine powers, [attains success]. || 102 ||
Year after year, he shall obtain the fruit of worshipping the sixty-four sacred seats (pīṭhas);
he shall attain the perfection of the command (ājñāsiddhi) and receive the favor of the deity. || 103 ||
He who, being previously acquainted with the ritual and knowing its procedure, performs the threefold worship consisting of will, knowledge, and action according to the method taught in the Āgamas.
One should properly satisfy the deities with ritual substances according to the extent of one's wealth; for when these three goddesses are satisfied, they bestow the fruits of all actions.
O Queen of Gods, they grant the desired objects of the practitioner—of this there is no doubt. (105)
Whoever performs the worship of these deities on special days according to the ritual of the weapon shall become dear to us both. 106.
He who, though capable, out of delusion does not worship the Śrīcakra on special festival days according to the Kaula tradition, shall become a beast for the Yoginīs.
Without the worship of the Kula, there is no authority whatsoever in the Cakra.
He who performs the Kula-worship with firm resolve is a Kaulika. 108.
If worship is performed without mantra, the deity is not pleased.
However, the Kaulika who performs the family worship (kulapūjā) with firm resolve, O Mistress of the Family (kuleśī), always attains union with the Yoginīs and the Heroes. 109.
Even a low-born person who performs the worship of the lineage even once with devotion attains a good rebirth; how much more so, then, other twice-born ones?
Therefore, with every effort, in all circumstances and at all times, one should be devoted to the worship of the Kula for the sake of attaining the desired fruit. (111)
Sacrifice is superior to family worship; a vow is superior to family worship;
a sacred ford is superior to family worship; and austerity is superior to family worship. (112)
Generosity that honors the family is supreme; action that honors the family is supreme;
knowledge that honors the family is supreme; and happiness that honors the family is supreme. 113.

The Dharma is superior to the worship of one's kin; the fruit is superior to the worship of one's kin; meditative absorption is superior to the worship of one's kin; and the great festival is superior to the worship of one's kin. (114)

The yoga that excels the worship of the family, the destiny that excels the worship of the family, the fortune that excels the worship of the family, and the adoration that excels the worship of the family. 115.
"It is not so, it is not so; again, it is not so! I swear this to you, O Mistress of the Family! What is the use of saying much more here? Listen to the secret, O Pārvatī! (116)
"O beautiful woman, know that I am present near you who performs the Kula worship according to the path taught in the Vedas and scriptures, and not elsewhere.
This is the truth, this is the truth; it is the truth, the truth—of this there is no doubt. (117)

O Beloved! O Goddess! The thousands of millions of Yoginīs who move through the air, the earth, the quarters, the waters, the mountains, and the forests, as well as an equal number of Bhairavas, have indeed been appointed by me for the protection of the Kula. 118.
Day after day, O Pārvatī, everyone with joyful faces gazes only at the practitioners out of a desire for their own worship.

When not honored, they create obstacles; when well-honored, they provide protection—[those who guard] those devoted to the guru, those of virtuous conduct, and those whose secret dharma is ever auspicious. (120)
O Dear One, because they destroy those who lack devotion and are of evil conduct, even though they may be teachers,
one should therefore meditate upon the Yoginīs and Bhairavas within the Śrīcakra.
If the foolish-minded one does not remember the Yoginīs, he becomes a *paśu* (a bound soul);
therefore, one should remember all the deities within the center of the Śrīcakra. 122.
O Goddess of the gods, they bestow grace upon practitioners; there is no doubt about this.
O Goddess, listen as I explain grace to you in its proper sequence. 123.
Whether for the sake of one's own benefit or for the benefit of others, [this rite] is most excellent and supreme;
it is performed with pure substances and accompanied by the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjā). || 124 ||
Having given the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to all of them, one should worship each of their individual fire-offering vessels;
they should be stationed according to their respective castes and adorned with all ornaments.
Filled with joy and bliss, each one individually self-composed and serene, they offered oblations consisting of milk-rice, clarified butter, and cooked grain, accompanied by devotion. || 126 ||
Having properly worshipped Gaṇeśvara with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, [one should recite]:
*hasakha phreṃ hesauṃ (hsauṃ) ḍāṃ ḍīṃ ḍamalavarayūṃ*. Then... 127.
O Dear One, having first uttered "Śrīpādukām" followed by "Hesau (hsau)," then "Hasakhaphreṃ," and enclosing these with the three sweets, one should mentally form the desired intention. 128.
Having properly worshipped each [deity] individually with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, O lotus-faced one, one should pray for one's desired wishes after having performed the worship. 129.
And the practitioner obtains all desired boons;
O Dear One, one should worship for the sake of protecting both oneself and others. 130.

For the purpose of destroying diseases, and just as here for the attainment of a son, for the sake of subjugation, for the sake of auspiciousness, and for the accomplishment of the goals of dharma and worldly prosperity. || 131 ||
O Goddess, one should worship for seven days, fourteen days, or twenty-one days; in this way, one obtains the desired fruit.
And one should give a separate sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), consisting of garments, ornaments, and a finger-ring, together with eight families and accompanied by sixty-four [attendants]. || 133 ||
Success occurs manifold through diligent practice of even that which has not been previously mastered; one should not practice stinginess with wealth if one desires success for oneself. (134)
Thus, O fair-faced one, the group of six has been fully described as a means of grace;
it should be practiced with effort by practitioners for the sake of attaining their own desired success. 135.
O fair-faced one, having meditated upon them, one should worship these [deities] beginning with the Ḍākinīs;
having worshipped the seventh goddess, one should worship her for the sake of attaining all accomplishments. (136)

"O you who have arisen from the body of Śakti! O you who eat the remains of Śakti’s offerings! Together with your own retinue, accept this offered remnant—[give] a pair [of garments], Svāhā! Thus is the disposal of the remains of the offering (nirmālya). || 137 ||
The Ḍākinī Sarpavadanā, born of wealth, possessing a blazing radiance, holds a water-pot and a knife, and bestows boons. (138)
The goddess Rākiṇī has the face of an owl, is blue in color, is equipped with a sword and a shield, and is adorned with all ornaments. || 139 ||
Lākinī is adorned with a glorious skull-bowl, holds a noose and a goad, is virtuous, resembles the pāṭalī flower in hue, and is decorated with all ornaments. (140)
Kākinī, who has the face of a horse and a luster like a ruby, possesses three faces adorned with severed heads; she is the bestower of success and is beautiful in every way. 141.
Śākinī resembles collyrium, has a feline face, and is most beautiful;
with a pure smile, she likewise holds a vajra and a staff.
Hākinī has the face of a bear and resembles a dark blue cloud;
she holds a skull and a trident in her hands and is adorned with shields.
She may have one, two, three, four, five, or six faces, and she is fearless like a lion.
Thus, O Mistress of the Kula, I have briefly described to you this particular worship for specific days; what more do you wish to hear? 144.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Worship on Special Days," in the *Ūrdhvāmnāya-tantra*, within the fifth section of the *Śrī Kulārṇava*, the great secret, the supreme among all scriptures, concerning the gateway to liberation and nirvāṇa, consisting of one hundred and twenty-five thousand verses. 10.
Now begins the eleventh chapter.
The Goddess said:
O Kuleśa, who are uniquely worshipped by all the worlds, I desire to hear [this].
O God, O ocean of compassion, tell me the sequence of the family traditions.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall declare that which you ask of me;
by the mere hearing of it, one is liberated from the bonds of the individual soul (paśu-pāśa).
If the eldest brother has been initiated but is devoid of the family worship and other such rites,
then the younger brother, provided he knows the Krama, shall perform the family worship.
Then, having gone near him and bowed to the Guru as is proper,
Pārvatī reported all of that to him and ate what remained.

During the midst of worship, when the Guru, an elder, or one worthy of honor has arrived, one should bow and say, "I am standing here"; then, having received permission, one should perform the remaining rites.
O Mistress of the Kula, when an elder and a younger disciple are staying together in one place,
the conduct [to be observed] therein has been explained as before.
When one who is ignorant of the Kaulika tradition has arrived, one should reflect upon the sequence of what precedes and follows;
O Goddess, having remembered one's own Guru, one should satisfy him according to one's own path.

One should perform the daily worship during the day and the occasional worship at night; the performance of rites for specific desires belongs to both times—such is the determination of the scripture. (8)

One should not perform the family worship (kulapūjā) without having bathed, nor while remaining seated, nor after eating, nor while talking idly; nor without being adorned with perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), auspicious garments, and so forth; nor without having properly composed the body. || 9 ||
O Dear One, it is said that worship without mantra, gratification without meat, and drinking without the power [of the mantra] are fruitless. (10)
One may perform the Śrīcakra alone, but one should not worship with a single vessel;
one should not worship with one hand, nor drink with one hand.
O Goddess, one should not worship with fish, meat, or fermented liquors in the presence of animals;
having prostrated, one should enter the cakra, and having prostrated again, one should depart.
O Dear One, one should not remain on a seat nor in the *vīrāsana* posture while at the *śrīcakra*.
O Goddess, upon seeing the *śrīcakra*, there is the destruction of the sins of the eyes;
if that [vision] is absent, then the pair of eyes of the *kaulika* is merely a pair of wounds. (13)

O Goddess, one should contemplate those who follow improper conduct, those of good conduct, those established in the *cakra*, and the *śakti-kaulikās* with the thought that they are Śiva and Gaurī; one should not despise them. 14.
Having gone to the house of the family preceptor, one should with devotion request for nectar-like food for the purification of sins; in its absence, one should drink water. || 15 ||
The disciple should receive the vessel given by the family preceptor according to his capacity and with devotion;
having offered salutations, he should accept it, for otherwise he would go to hell. || 16 ||
O Mistress of the Kula, he who partakes of the Kula-substance without having bathed, or without devotion, or even out of greed, shall surely encounter poverty. (17)

One who wears a turban, one wearing a bodice, one who is naked, one with disheveled hair, one surrounded by a crowd, one who is distracted, angry, or argumentative—such a person should not partake of the nectar of the family (kulāmṛta). || 18 ||
By spitting the nectar of yoga due to wandering about with a vessel of liquor, and by drinking it through an upward-pointing tube, one incurs the curse of the deities. (19)
O beloved, those who sit upon a single seat while eating from a single vessel,
and drink substances from a single bowl, go to hell.

O Maheśānī, he who should consume the family property while the Guru, a kinsman of that lineage, his son, his own elder brother, or the family preceptor resides in the same village, would go to an inexhaustible hell without their permission. (21)
O Pārvatī, one who is impure from eating should not touch the ritual substances of the Kula within the maṇḍala;
having washed his hands outside, he should then offer the Kula substances.
O Dear One, having removed the vessel for intoxicants, one should not fill the drinking bowl;
one should never cast the vessel for enjoyment into the vat of liquor.
That foolish-minded person who performs the washing of hands and other such acts with a mind of impurity in the center of the *cakra* shall indeed become a vessel for calamities. (24)
He who performs spitting, excreting waste, urinating, or releasing downward wind within the center of the Śrīcakra shall become a beast for the Yoginīs. || 25 ||
O Dear One, when the wheel is broken, the jar is shattered, or the vessel falls to the ground,
and when the lamp is extinguished, one should cause the Śrīcakra to be made for the sake of pacification.
O Beloved, the wise ones mutter prayers, meditate, offer praise, and bow down; they awaken [others], inquire, and rejoice (27).
Intoxicated, they wander about, roar, laugh, and quarrel;
they weep, desire women, and revile others, O beloved—such are the ignorant. (28)
One should avoid joking, idle chatter, cavil, excessive speech,
indifference, fear, and anger while in the midst of the circle.
O Great Goddess, one should not wander through the midst of the maṇḍala with a vessel in hand;
O Beloved, having taken a full vessel in one's hand, one should not remain there for long.
One should not speak while holding the bowl in one's hand, nor should one break the bowl, O Ambikā;
one should not touch the bowl with one's feet, nor let a drop fall to the ground.
O Dear One, one should not give with only one hand, nor should one be devoid of the mudrā;
one should not move the bowl from its place, nor should one cause a mixing of bowls.
One should not drink liquor making a noise, nor should one fill [the vessel] to the brim;
one should not strike one vessel against another, nor should one let it fall to the ground. (33)
One should not lift a vessel that has no base, nor should one place it on something that lacks a base.
One should not leave a vessel empty, nor, O beloved, should one swing the vessel about.
The wise one should not leap over the vessel, nor should he shake the vessel, O beloved;
having washed it, he should conceal the vessel—this is the command of the Supreme Goddess. (35)
When the Kaulika, his [inner] splendor fully ignited, beholds a bound soul (paśu), or recites the scriptures of the bound, or associates with the wife of a bound soul; (36)
If one indulges in sexual intercourse with animals or performs acts pertaining to animals, then dharma, wealth, longevity, fame, merit, prosperity, happiness, and so forth, will perish. (37)
He who gives the *kuladravya* situated within the *śrīcakra* to the uninitiated (*paśus*), whether out of affection, greed, or even fear, shall become a *yoginī-paśu*. (38)
One should not engage in verbal dispute even with an enemy while in the midst of the assembly;
one should regard him as equal to a father or mother and endure the harsh words spoken by him.
Just as the mind rejoices upon seeing a woman, a son, a friend, or the like, so too if it rejoices upon seeing Kaulikas, he shall be beloved by the Yoginīs. (40)
He whose lineage of gurus extends from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, and who is my disciple—whom on this earth would he not honor?
He who possesses such a resolute intellect shall be dear to us both. (41)
Those who proclaim, "I am the guru, I am the elder,
I alone know," and "I alone am their refuge," are not true Kaulikas.
O Goddess, having bowed with devotion to the venerable Guru, the Kula scriptures, and whatever places of worship there may be, one should praise them while prefixing their names with the word "Śrī."
O Dear One, one should not address the Guru by name except at the time of recitation;
in debate or during spiritual practice, one should say "Śrīnātha," "Devam," or "Svāmī."
O Goddess of the Gods, one should not disclose the sandals of the Śrī Guru, the mudrā, the root mantra, or one's own sandals to anyone other than the disciple—to whomever it may be. (45)
O Dear One, the traditional lineage of transmission, including the mantras, rituals, and so forth, becomes fruitful only when obtained from the mouth of a guru, and not otherwise. (46)
O Dear One, one should not speak of this book, which has its root in the refuge of the Śrīśāstra;
one should always worship it with devotion and never place it in the hand of an uninitiated person (paśu). || 47 ||
O Pārvatī, one should follow the Kula scriptures as one does one's own wife;
one should avoid all Paśu scriptures as one would another's wife. (48)
Just as milk contained within its own hide is unfit to be drunk by the best of the twice-born,
so too the Dharma from the mouth of a beast must not be heard by the Kaulikas.
He who hears the family tradition and he who speaks it according to the scriptures—both of them go directly to the assembly of the Yoginīs and the Vīras. (50)
O Mistress of the Family, those who lack faith here in this family dharma do not return from hell until the dissolution of the world at the end of the kalpa.
A wife who has been wedded, one who has been supported, one who has been purchased with a price, one who has been brought together through wealth,
or even one who has once experienced sexual pleasure— these five types of a teacher’s wives are as inviolable and worthy of worship as the teacher himself. (52)
One should not desire the power of the Guru, the wife of a hero, a maiden, one who observes a vow, nor one with deformed limbs, disfigured limbs, or even a hunchbacked woman.
One should not desire a daughter, a sister, a granddaughter, or even a beloved daughter-in-law in the presence of one's guru; nor should one engage in mutual socializing with them.
One should worship her— who is clad in black garments, dark-complexioned, a young maiden with a slender waist, enchanting, and in the prime of youth— with the thought that she is the deity herself.
One should never, even once, approach a Kula-yoginī by force;
O beautiful lady of the Kula, one should desire her only when she herself is stirred within the center of the Cakra.
Raw meat, a jar of liquor, an intoxicated elephant, a perfected ascetic, a mango tree, an aśoka tree, and young maidens eager for play. (57)
Upon seeing a single tree, a cremation ground, a gathering of women, or even a woman dressed in red garments, one should pay homage with devotion. (58)
The gurus, the Śaktis, the sons, the elders, and the juniors; the Kula-teachers, the scriptures of the Kula-darśana, the Kula-substances, and the Kaulikas.
[He saw] those who incite, those who indicate, as well as those who recite,
those who show, teachers, enlighteners, yogis, and those who assist in the accomplishment of the yoginīs.
One should not revile, nor loathe, nor laugh at, nor insult a maiden, a young girl, or even a woman who is naked or insane.
One should not speak unpleasantly or falsely to any member of a family of yogis. Nor should one call a woman of such a family "ugly" or "black. (62)
One should not examine the deeds or omissions of devoted heroes;
nor should one look upon a naked woman, one who is insane, or one whose breasts are exposed.
On that day, he should not take pleasure with a woman, nor should he even look upon her womb;
whatever woman there may be in the world, she is born from the lineage of his mother.
The noble *kulayoginīs* become enraged by the transgressions of women;
even if a woman has committed a hundred offenses, one should not strike her even with a flower.
One should not enumerate the faults of women, but rather manifest their virtues alone. (65)
The Kula-yoginīs always reside within the Kula-trees;
one must not eat from their leaves, but should worship them especially. (66)
One should not sleep at the foot of a family tree, nor should one cause it harm;
having seen it, one should bow with devotion, and never cut it down.
Śleṣmātaka, the one called Karañja, Nimba, Aśvattha, Kadambaka, Bilva, Vaṭa, Udumbara, and Tintiḍī is recorded as the ninth. (68)
A Kaula should avoid these five: performing penance, falling from a cliff, renunciation, observing vows, and undertaking pilgrimages.
The killing of a hero, the drinking of intoxicants in vain, consorting with the wife of a hero,
the theft of a hero’s property, and association with those who commit these acts— these five are declared to be the great sins (*mahāpātaka*) within the Kula lineage of the Kaulikas. (70)
In the Śaiva [tantra], the thorough knowledge of the principles (tattvas) is the essence; in the Gāruḍa, the consumption of poison;
in Jyotiṣa, the planetary eclipses; and in the Kaula, the powers of grace and restraint.
One who mocks the deities, the guru, and the scriptures, or who violates established conduct; a thief of knowledge and a traitor to the guru, shall become a *brahmarākṣasa*. (72)
O beloved, by disregarding the words of the Guru and reviling the heroes;
by uttering "huṃ" and "tuṃ" at the Guru, or by defeating a hero in debate;
and by casting doubt upon the Kula scriptures, they become Brahma-rākṣasas. (73)
He who treats with contempt the Guru who has bestowed upon him even a single syllable shall pass through a hundred births as a dog and then attain the state of a Caṇḍāla. || 74 ||
O Goddess, one should indeed slay without hesitation a mother, a father, a wife, a brother, a kinsman, or a son who brings disgrace upon the family. 75.

For the sake of the Guru, or for the sake of the Deity, O Mistress of Kula; or for the sake of the Kaulika purpose, or for the sake of the Kula scripture, or indeed for the sake of the Kula dharma. (76)
O Goddess, he who, having slain one who reviles him or even when himself oppressed,
should abandon his life which is so difficult to give up, merges into the supreme Śiva.
When a single evildoer is brought to his end, there is security for many; merit arises from his killing. (78)
"O Supreme Goddess, it is the command that one must never speak of the events concerning the Śrīcakra, whether they be auspicious or inauspicious. (79)
O beloved, one should never engage in the recitation of the family dharma in front of animals,
nor ever before a Śūdra, just as one would not recite the names of the gods.

O Goddess, one should not speak of the sacred seats (pīṭha), fields (kṣetra), scriptures (āgama), and traditions (āmnāya), nor of those who practice that vidyā and the Kaulikas, nor of the substances of the Kula and so forth, in the presence of a paśu.
